result.text: Investigator-assessed median PFS 7.6 months (95% CI 5.6, 10.2) with mogamulizumab vs 3.1 months (95% CI 2.8, 4.0) with vorinostat; HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.41, 0.69; p<0.0001). Confirmed ORR per investigator 28% vs 5% (p<0.0001).

citations.quote: Investigator-assessed progression-free survival (PFS) was statistically significantly longer in the mogamulizumab arm (median 7.6 months; 95% CI: 5.6, 10.2) than in the vorinostat arm (median 3.1 months; 95% CI, 2.8, 4.0), with a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.53 (95% CI: 0.41, 0.69; 2-sided stratified log rank test p<0.0001).
The confirmed objective response rate (ORR) per investigator was statistically significantly (p<0.0001) higher for mogamulizumab (28%) than for vorinostat (5%).

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were rash, infusion related reactions, fatigue, diarrhea, musculoskeletal pain, and upper respiratory tract infection. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 36% (66/184), most often infection (16%). Fatal adverse reactions within 90 days occurred in 2.2% (7/319). Fatal and life-threatening skin reactions including SJS and TEN, and immune-mediated complications, have occurred.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (reported in ≥20% of patients) were rash, infusion related reactions, fatigue, diarrhea, musculoskeletal pain, and upper respiratory tract infection [6.1].
Serious adverse reactions were reported in 36% (66/184) of patients randomized to POTELIGEO and most often involved infection (16% of patients; 30/184).
Fatal adverse reactions within 90 days of the last dose occurred in 2.2% (7/319) of patients who received POTELIGEO as randomized or crossover treatment.
Fatal and life-threatening skin adverse reactions, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), have occurred in recipients of POTELOGEO.
Fatal and life-threatening immune-mediated complications have been reported in recipients of POTELIGEO.

detail.text: The clinical review team did not recommend a REMS; safety issues can be adequately managed through labeling and routine post-marketing surveillance.
